Prgm
    { prgmObjMap = ObjectMapWith
        { omItems = fromList
            [
                ( "/ContextIn"
                , ObjectMapItem
                    { omiDecls = []
                    , omiRuntimeDecls =
                        [ /ContextIn
                            ( EAppArg
                                { eaaArg = Value /value -> /System/env( /name=/Catln/CStr ) = /System/env
                                    ( EAppArg { eaaArg = Value /name -> /Catln/CStr } )
                                }
                            )
                            ( EAppArg
                                { eaaArg = Value /ctx -> ( /io=/Catln/IO ).. = /
                                    ( EAppArg { eaaArg = Value /io -> /Catln/IO } )
                                    ( EAppSpread
                                        { easExpr = Hole TopType HoleActive { haName = Nothing } }
                                    )
                                }
                            ) -> /Context
                            ( /value=∀/Data/Maybe[ /T=∀/Data/String ]
                            , /ctx=( /io=/Catln/IO )..
                            )
                        ]
                    , omiRefineDecls = []
                    , omiDefs = []
                    }
                )
            ]
        , omDecls = []
        }
    , prgmCg = [ CGType ]
    , prgmAnnots =
        [ /Catln/#md
            ( EAppArg
                { eaaArg = Value /text ->
                    ( /Data/String/Text
                        ( /chars=∀/Data/List/ConsList[ /T=/Data/Char ] ).. + /Catln/CStr
                    ) = "# Environment
                  What a program can read of the environment it was started in. It runs in an [/Catln/IO]
                  context because it reaches outside the program: a run started with different variables set
                  answers differently, so reading one is an effect, and a program can only do it where it runs in
                  an io.
                  This is not part of the standard library. A program which reads no variable has no use for it,
                  and one that does writes `import "env"`."
                }
            )
        ]
    }
